findings.desc: CHK-011:adversarial:1 evidence mismatch: intent is "Remove the chain-smoke from validate.commands -> lattice validate no longer runs it; the regression must be caught by a committed test or the validate output audit" (i.e. detect de-registration of red-evidence-chain-smoke.js from lattice.config.json validate.commands). The bound evidence is packages/main/tests/red/red-w2c-wiring-detectability.mjs, which tests a DIFFERENT scenario entirely: stripping the compiled command-policy.js registration entry for red_evidence_quarantine/red_evidence_recover and asserting command-ownership-contract/lifecycle-registry-contract fail. It never touches lattice.config.json validate.commands nor red-evidence-chain-smoke.js at all. No committed test in the repo scans validate.commands for completeness against packages/main/src/tasks/*.ts, so removing the chain-smoke registration line from lattice.config.json today would go undetected by any committed mechanism. Note this same wiring-detectability test IS a strong match for CHK-011:adversarial:0's intent ("delete the command-catalog entry for red_evidence_quarantine"), suggesting the evidence binder cross-assigned it to the wrong intentRef and left adversarial:1 genuinely uncovered.

CHK-001:edge:0 evidence is weaker than the sibling coverage in the same file. Intent: "Construct a green-confirm record; verify it has confirmsRecordId/confirmsRecordDigest/confirmsAssertionDigest but NO assertion/policySnapshot of its own". red-evidence-chain-smoke.ts section 1 (lines 180-197) proves this EXACT pattern for the quarantine record by hand-building a draft object and asserting field presence/absence with the `in` operator in a loop. For green-confirm (CHK-001:edge:0) the smoke never constructs a GreenConfirmRecordV2 instance at all -- it only calls greenConfirmOperationKey() (a function over primitive strings) and checks the GRN- id prefix (lines 333/338). The claim that this is adequate because "the field set is the compiled discriminated-union contract (green-confirm writer is W2e)" relies purely on TypeScript type erasure at compile time; nothing at runtime confirms a constructed green-confirm object omits assertion/policySnapshot the way the quarantine test does two sections above it. Building a synthetic GreenConfirmRecordV2 draft (as was already done for red-assert and quarantine, which also have no writer command registered by this story) and running the same `in`-based presence/omission loop would have been directly achievable without needing the W2e writer, and would match the sibling evidence quality used for every other operation in this same section.

packages/main/src/core/proofstory.ts:944 redEvidenceRecordSatisfied guards only isRedEvidenceV2(record) (exact schemaVersion==="proofstory.red_evidence.v2"); any record whose schemaVersion is set but NOT that exact string (a future v3, or a corrupted/malformed stored record) falls through to the v1 branch and crashes at record.observedFailure.trim() (:947-949) in the LIVE enforce gate — reproduced live: writing {schemaVersion:"proofstory.red_evidence.v3", operation:"red-assert", ...} (no observedFailure) into a real store and calling evaluateProofStoryDiagnostics throws TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading trim). This contradicts CHK-003s own title (skip EVERY non-v1 record) and the forward-compatibility fail-closed philosophy record-v2.ts:177 classifyRedRecordSchema documents (throws on unknown schemaVersion) — but classifyRedRecordSchema is never called from the gate path (only from its own smoke-test assertion in red-evidence-chain-smoke.ts:200-203), so the fail-closed guarantee it advertises is not actually wired to the one place (the live enforce gate) that the story exists to protect. RED signal A is fixed only for the specific known-v2 shape, not for the non-v1/non-v2 case its own doc comments claim to cover.

packages/main/src/core/red-evidence/record-v2.ts:177-188 classifyRedRecordSchema (the CHK-002 adversarial fail-closed-on-unknown-schemaVersion guarantee) is declared and unit-tested in isolation but is NEVER CALLED from any real read path: store.ts:852 readRedEvidence does plain JSON.parse with zero validation, and proofstory.ts:944 redEvidenceRecordSatisfied only skips records whose schemaVersion is the LITERAL string proofstory.red_evidence.v2 (via isRedEvidenceV2) -- any OTHER/unknown schemaVersion (e.g. proofstory.red_evidence.v3, or a typo/corrupted value) falls through to the v1 branch and crashes at record.observedFailure.trim() (proofstory.ts:945) because such a record has no observedFailure field. Live-reproduced against the built dist: a red-evidence.json record {schemaVersion:proofstory.red_evidence.v3, id:RED-v3-1, operation:quarantine, ...} (no observedFailure) is silently accepted into records[] and then throws TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading trim) inside evaluateProofStoryDiagnostics -> redEvidenceSatisfied -> .some(redEvidenceRecordSatisfied), i.e. it crashes the LIVE dev/review/done enforce gate (devGateMode/reviewGateMode/doneGateMode all enforce). This directly contradicts CHK-002 adversarial:0 (a record with an unknown schemaVersion is rejected at parse/load time with a diagnostic, not silently accepted into the array) and reopens, for any non-v2 schema drift, the EXACT crash class (record.observedFailure.trim() on a fieldless control record) that CHK-003/RED-signal-A in this same story was built to close for v2 specifically. The only test exercising classifyRedRecordSchema (red-evidence-chain-smoke.ts:200-203) calls it directly as a standalone function, never through store.readRedEvidence or the actual gate pipeline, so the gap is untested end-to-end.
